extracted.intended_audience: Prospective proposers/performers preparing Solution Summaries and Full Proposals for the ARPA-H PROSPR program (academic, industry, and consortium teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing Solution Summaries and Full Proposals in response to the ARPA-H PROSPR Innovative Solutions Opening, including budget, team composition, technical approaches for TA1/TA2/TA3, data/IP expectations, and submission formatting. Covers eligibility, templates, timelines, and technical expectations for each Technical Area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find solicitation details
rubrics_metrics.description: You can find all of the relevant details on SAM.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the solicitation on SAM.gov and the Innovative Solutions Opening (ISO) for full information; SAM.gov hosts the ISO and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget must reflect true costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget submitted should be representative of the costs required to perform the work proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers are encouraged to submit a budget commensurate with the proposed work and include sufficient back-up information for the government to understand basis of the budget; include all reasonable direct and indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing expectation despite IP
rubrics_metrics.description: We support companies having IP, however we do expect data sharing for the overall gain of the program. For example, biomarkers would have to be shared as part of the program as this is a government-funded program that is meant to benefit all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers may retain IP but must plan for data/biomarker sharing that supports program-wide goals; clarify in proposal how sharing will occur while addressing IP protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: No per-TA budget cap
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not a budget cap or expected range for each TA. Proposers are encouraged to submit their best ideas with a commensurate budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume an upper budget limit; justify requested funds relative to scope and deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award decisions based on best proposal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: We will award funding to the team/teams that present the best proposal and provide the most evidence they will be effective in accomplishing their goals independent of the number of teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are evaluated on merit and evidence of capability; multiple awards are anticipated but quality of proposal drives selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: International teams and overseas work allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, please see Section 6.1.2 of the Draft ISO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign participation is permitted but must be disclosed per ISO and Volume III requirements; follow foreign participation disclosure guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on team size, but clear value required
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the size of teams, but each member should provide clear value and be managed by at least one Prime proposer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure teams so each member’s role and value are explicit; prime must demonstrate management structure and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime may serve as sub-prime elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Can a prime submitter also submit as a sub-prime in another effort? Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities may appear in multiple roles across proposals; ensure compliance with submission/prime limits at full proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposers must provide their own CRO if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers are responsible for proposing a team capable of meeting all PROSPR Program requirements. CRO services will not be provided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CRO services are necessary for execution, include them in team composition and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task tabs correspond to Technical Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task tabs refer to specific Technical Areas (e.g., Task Tab 1 = TA 1). Proposers must fill out the applicable Task tabs based on the number of TAs included in their proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Task tabs only for TAs included; Phase tabs roll up all proposed TAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year columns are proposer's FY
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiscal years are the proposer’s fiscal years. Proposers may unhide columns as necessary if the Phase (base, option, etc.) extends beyond a single FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your organization’s fiscal year for budget timelines and adjust spreadsheet columns if phases span multiple FYs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include direct and indirect costs; no separate financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: No financial assistance will be issued as a result of the PROSPR solicitation. Proposers are encouraged to submit a budget that is reasonable and consistent with the technical approach. Thus, budgets should include all reasonable costs (direct and indirect) with sufficient back-up information for the government to understand the basis of the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare cost proposals assuming contractual fixed-amount Other Transaction Agreements; include full burdened rates and supporting documentation in Cost and Pricing Data Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHHS salary cap likely not applicable; provide fully burdened labor rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The DHHS salary cap will likely not apply to PROSPR awards because the government intends to award fixed amount Other Transaction Agreements and has requested only fully burdened labor rates in the Cost Proposal spreadsheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fully burdened labor rates; do not assume DHHS cap applies unless otherwise notified during negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No release of past redacted proposals/budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: The government will not release redacted past submissions, including budget submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect example redacted proposals from the government; submit specific process/questions to PROSPR@arpa-h.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior communication with ARPA-H not required
rubrics_metrics.description: No (it is not necessary to establish communication with your team prior to applying for PROSPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may contact program email for specific questions, but pre-submission communication is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed start date for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may use an assumed start date of 1 DEC 2025 as a start date in their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 12/1/25 for planning; the government may update date during negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel multiple-performer awards possible but proposals should meet full requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: While the government has the right to select portions of a proposal for award negotiations, the expectation is that proposals will include a technical solution that meets all TA/track requirements established in the ISO. Teaming is encouraged as/if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design proposals to fully satisfy TA/track requirements even if expecting partial awards; clarify how teaming will enable delivery of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget for participant travel and in-person assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, the Performer should propose the budget for in person assessments. Proposer budgets should account for all aspects of the proposer’s intended SOW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include travel costs for participants to clinics or for staff to visit homes as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cost for testing kits and scale-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, proposer budgets should account for all aspects of the proposer’s intended SOW, including testing kits for their own study (of 1K participants + N to compensate for attrition) and an additional 3K kits to scale the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget kits both for initial study and anticipated scaling; justify quantities and attrition assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget template on SAM.gov is for full proposal only
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget template on SAM.Gov is for the full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the budget template with the Solution Summary; use it for Full Proposal submission only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include ROM/BOE in Solution Summary per Appendix B Section F
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refer to the Appendix B, Section F: Rough Order of Magnitude of the PROSPR ISO for ROM/BOE requirements. This section should be included with the other sections of the Solution Summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a separate ROM/BOE table as required by Appendix B Section F to summarize total costs and high-level breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Labor vs Labor Hours reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: In the provided template, direct labor is referring to the labor category. The labor hours are the hours associated with the labor category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report labor hours by labor category per phase; use Basis of Estimate cells for justification where provided; include Cost and Pricing Data Support in Cost Proposal Volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract cost breakout in Cost Proposal Volume II
rubrics_metrics.description: See Appendix C, Volume II information (Section b. Cost Proposal Spreadsheet) for guidance on subcontract cost breakdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide subcontractor-level cost details per Appendix C requirements where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative point of contact definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative point of contact is intended to be someone who is responsible for the non-technical aspects of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign an administrative POC within your team responsible for submission logistics and contractual matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team member identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You should list all entities involved, including 1099 consultants. Team members for the purpose of this section include all entities (e.g., prime, subawardee(s), and consultant(s)) who will be supplying research, components, information, data, or material that is critical to your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each entity (including employer entity for PIs) and include role descriptions; do not omit consultants/1099s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign participation disclosures include all individuals on team
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign participation disclosures, 'proposed team members' encompasses all individuals of any entity on the team, not limited to those in PI or Senior/Key Personnel roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose foreign national participation at the individual and entity level as required in Volume III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding mechanism: contractual agreements (OTAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide funding in the form of contractual agreements for performers carrying out negotiated research and development work relevant to the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) contracting mechanism; include deliverables, milestones, and negotiated terms in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submission rules and PI roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see Section 5.1 of the Draft ISO for guidelines on multiple submissions. In particular, limitations on being PI/co-PI/co-investigator across proposals are governed by the ISO and Section 5.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Section 5.1 for specifics; generally an entity may be prime on only one full proposal, but may be subprime on multiple proposals and individuals may appear in multiple roles per ISO guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portal and ISO references
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPR is independent from the Mission Office ISOs, and the ARPA-H solutions portal will be used. Please see Section 4.2 of the Draft ISO for Solution Summary submission information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Solution Summaries via ARPA-H solutions portal per Section 4.2; follow portal file upload guidance (Task Description Document/Research Description Document mapping to SOWs allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: OT Bundle of Attachments and templates release timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The OT Bundle of Attachments, which contains relevant templates, will be released no later than with the Final ISO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates from the OT Bundle for Full Proposal when available; Appendix C and Model OT provide SOW and milestone templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open call and PROSPR dual submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to submit to both, however, awarded work cannot have overlapping scope. It is recommended to submit to the Program ISO if that is a fit for your proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overlapping scope across awards; clearly delineate scope if submitting to multiple solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly-traded entities eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly traded companies are eligible to apply for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is defined by ISO scope; include necessary disclosures and corporate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution Summary selection process and feedback timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers will first submit a Solution Summary. These will be reviewed by the PROSPR team and a subset will be encouraged to submit a full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government will provide encouragement feedback as quickly as possible, but timing depends on number of submissions; only encouraged Solution Summaries proceed to Full Proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical and written abstract single-page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphical and written abstract must be on a single page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine graphical and written abstract content to one page; adhere to formatting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Organization and Capabilities page counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Team Organization and Capabilities section should be within the 5-page Proposed work section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place Team Org & Capabilities outside of the 5-page Proposed work; ensure required elements fit within page constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font size minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: The font size should be no smaller than 11-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all narrative text meets the 11-point minimum; adhere to other formatting rules in ISO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution Summaries are selection-sensitive/confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Solution Summaries and proposals are considered Selection Sensitive and not shared publicly. Submissions are only shared internally to the extent required to fulfill the Scientific Review process. Those who require access are either federal employees or support contractors who have signed appropriate Non-Disclosure Agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Solution Summaries as confidential; do not expect public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: References are outside 5-page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: As listed in the General Instructions of Appendix B, any references provided are outside of the 5-page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include reference lists without counting against the 5-page Proposed work limit; follow Appendix B formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI and active SAM registration required at full proposal stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to have a UEI and active SAM registration applies at the full proposal stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure organizational registrations (UEI, SAM) are active before submitting Full Proposal; not required for Solution Summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaming structure may change between Solution Summary and Full Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposing team may revise its teaming structure between Solution Summary submission and the full proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If teaming changes, ensure Full Proposal accurately reflects new team and capabilities; governmental review at Solution Summary stage is based on information provided then.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAGE/NCAGE code not required
rubrics_metrics.description: No (a CAGE/NCAGE code is not required for submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume CAGE is mandatory unless later requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission limit as prime applies only to full proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission limit applies to full proposals only. Each institution is allowed to submit one full proposal to the PROSPR program as prime regardless of the number of TAs included in the full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primes may only be prime on one Full Proposal; they may be subprime on multiple Full Proposals; Solution Summary stage does not count toward this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume I (technical) page guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bottom of Volume I information is a summary of proposal elements recommended for inclusion in proposals based on each TA and track proposed, as well as recommendations for all proposals. These elements should be incorporated into the 30-page Volume I submission however the proposer deems most appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate recommended technical elements into Volume I's 30 pages; consult page 46 and Appendix C for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch and Other Support certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, Biosketches and Other Support must be signed and certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use referenced biosketch forms and ensure signatures/certifications per ISO (link provided in ISO page 59).

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 PROSPR-IC composition and allowable measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, the improved IC score should include all five components of IC, but can include other physiological and biochemical parameters providing they improve the accuracy of 20 year health outcomes. Omics as well as routine lab work can be considered as the additional biochemical measures, please see section 2.3.1 of the draft ISO for more details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design PROSPR-IC to include core five components plus justified additions; use evidence to show improvements in long-term outcome prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 proxies of IC physiological components generally not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, we will not allow proxies of IC physiological components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where ISO expects direct measurement (e.g., grip strength, MOCA), propose direct assessments unless you provide compelling justification accepted during negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 biochemical sampling frequency flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The biochemical components can be measured at regular intervals of your choosing, providing you adequately justify the timing in your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify sampling frequency scientifically and balance with cost targets (e.g., $100 IC assessment goal).

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 in-home vs clinic visits
rubrics_metrics.description: The intention of the clinic visits is to ensure that the in-home measures accurately reflect Intrinsic Capacity measures taken in the clinic or by a medical professional. Sending a professional to the home could replace clinic visits, but we find it unlikely this could be a fully virtual approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan in-person clinic assessments or medically supervised home visits to validate in-home measures; fully virtual assessment likely insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 sample size and trial structure guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be approximately 1000 participants in the observational trial, from which a subset should be used in the lifestyle intervention trial. Please propose the number of participants required based on a statistical power analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design power analyses for primary endpoints and attrition; justify numbers and whether subset transitions to intervention trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 device cost target
rubrics_metrics.description: The final device cost of less than $100 for the consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design assessment devices/systems with per-consumer or per-use cost under ~$100; amortize device costs within reason and justify amortization period.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 allowance for omics but cost considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it acceptable to include mRNA as part of the PROSPR IC score for TA1, given that it is excluded from TA2a? It is not expressly excluded. However, given the cost associated with mRNA sample collection and testing, it is unlikely that the benefits to a predictive score outweigh the risk of not adhering to $100 cost for IC assessment in place of other biomarkers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing expensive omics, show cost-benefit and how IC assessment still meets cost targets or justify exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA1 metric harmonization requirement (95% consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISO mentions that 'data cleaning, normalization, and validation are performed to ensure at least 95% consistency across datasets.' 95% consistency applies to shared or comparable variables across datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scientifically defendable metrics and validation methods to demonstrate harmonized variables achieve ~95% consistency; apply consistency independently to overlapping variable subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2b participant age and endpoints expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The metrics specify a clinical trial with participants who are 60 years old. Does this mean every participant must start the trial at 60, or is a range permitted? Yes, a range of participants ages will be permitted. Clarification will be available in the final ISO. It is expected that you propose primary endpoints for TA2b in addition to the PROSPR IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose appropriate age ranges and primary endpoints with strong scientific rationale and evidence; include justification in Solution Summary and Full Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2 repurposed drugs and FDA pathway expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, FDA-repurposed drugs that are not listed in the ISO as examples acceptable if rationale supports aging. TA2 and TA3 are required to seek FDA approval for interventions. A label change typically requires the original NDA holder to submit data to the FDA; ARPA-H is not aware of alternative approved mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For repurposing, address regulatory path, IND/IDE needs, partnerships with NDA holders if label change sought, and timeline to approval in proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2b can propose multiple drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have two drugs, you may propose both in one proposal and please let the budget reflect your intention to test two, rather than a single, drug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and design trials to accommodate multiple arms/drugs and power accordingly; describe selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2b hybrid trials permitted and technology integration
rubrics_metrics.description: For TA2b, hybrid trials are permitted. TA2b performers will provide the assessment technology to the TA2b decentralized trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design hybrid trial operational plans that meet IND/IRB requirements and ensure assessment tech integrates with TA1 where needed; include drug-only arm if including lifestyle interventions to maximize FDA approval chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2b timeline expectations for IND/IRB and recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISO expects performers to apply for IRB in Phase I and to have received approval early in Phase II. However, proposers should propose the timeline they believe will ensure the success of their Solution. IRB approval must occur before patients are recruited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose realistic timelines for IRB/IND processes and recruitment; be prepared to negotiate timelines if selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2 trial start and availability of drug
rubrics_metrics.description: For TA2, when does the repurposed drug need to be available for the trial? The trial begins at the start of year 3 of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan drug supply and regulatory readiness so investigational product is available by Year 3 start; include manufacturing/supply considerations in budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA2 participant eligibility health criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should be in general good health, aged 60-65, without diagnosed diseases such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define inclusion/exclusion criteria that align with ISO guidance; justify any deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA3 expectation for preclinical in vivo data
rubrics_metrics.description: For TA3, please ensure that the Solution Summary contains all of the in-vivo data available for your intervention, particularly data that demonstrates preserved health in aged animals or other in-vivo justification to perform such studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide existing preclinical in vivo evidence (mammalian preferred) showing preserved health or lifespan/healthspan improvements; remaining studies should be proposed as part of TA3 phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA3 requirement to propose full TA3 (preclinical through clinical)
rubrics_metrics.description: No, TA3 performers must propose the entirety of TA3 from preclinical to clinical trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit TA3-only preclinical plans unless you include proposed clinical translation phases; teams cannot defer Phase 1b until after selection without proposing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA3 animal model restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: At this time, we will focus on interventions that increase healthspan in the environment of natural aging and therefore will not allow genetically modified animals in the PROSPR program. Exceptions to the rodent model proposed may be considered in cases where preliminary data strongly suggests the therapeutic will extend healthspan in non-disease contexts and justification is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use naturally aged mammalian models where possible; provide strong justification for alternative models and consult amendment language for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA3 complementary assays allowed if IC included
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, you are permitted to include any analysis that would demonstrate preserved health over time in your Solution Summary/Proposal provided IC is also included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include IC as required primary metric; additional assays (immune, muscle, electrophysiology, etc.) may be proposed and will be negotiated if selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: TA3 device interventions read IDE not IND
rubrics_metrics.description: If we plan to apply for TA3 with a medical device, should we read IND as IDE for a solution summary? Yes, you should read IDE instead of IND when applying for TA3 with a medical device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address device regulatory pathway (IDE) where applicable and include relevant preclinical/device testing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of interventions not limited to pharmacologic
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed interventions are not required to be pharmacological. A goal of the PROSPR program is build a healthspan therapeutic industry, therefore we require TA2 and TA3 to seek FDA approval for their interventions. Lifestyle interventions are suitable for TA1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match intervention types to TA expectations: TA1 lifestyle/measurement work, TA2/TA3 interventions aimed at FDA pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization planning expectations vary by TA
rubrics_metrics.description: We understand that some TAs will have more comprehensive commercialization requirements than others. For example, TA2b commercialization plan could address how the data produced might be used by commercial entities or more support the commercialization goals of the PROSPR IC, or how a repurposed drug would enter the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a commercialization plan proportional to TA objectives and expected deliverables; be specific about market pathway, partners, and cost-to-consumer assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposer responsibility for justifying capability and potential hires
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a proposer’s responsibility how it substantiates its capability to meet the requirements of its proposed technical approach. Hiring someone as project manager is acceptable but the government’s ability to assess capability depends on information in the full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of current capability, key personnel, or plausible hiring plans and explain how potential hires will be onboarded and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and power analysis guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should recruit the number of participants such that at the end of the study, you are sufficiently powered, taking into consideration participant attrition or exclusion throughout the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include power analyses, assumptions on attrition, and plans to over-recruit if needed; justify statistical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics: trial-specific vs aggregated approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally this metric is robust per individual trial, but we recognize the level of high variability. We purposely did not prescribe whether it should be per individual trial or aggregated analyses. We suggest you address the best approach in your full proposal and make sure its justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether your analytic plan evaluates IC improvements per trial or across pooled analyses and justify based on statistical reasoning and harmonization ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant eligibility for intervention selection from observational cohort
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it acceptable to recruit the subset of participants from the observational study to be those of lower IC? Yes, this is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide selection criteria and justify subset selection methods; ensure IRB/consent accommodates transition from observational to intervention arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinic assessments can be performed by in-home clinicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Any medical professional that would typically assess or conduct the assessments in the clinic is acceptable for the clinic assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for qualified medical personnel to conduct clinic-equivalent assessments during home visits where justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and ISO errata notes (Appendix D reference error)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements for the full proposal (Volumes I, II, and III) are clearly outlined in Appendix C. Please note the reference to ‘Appendix D’ is in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Appendix C and Model OT templates; use Model OT for SOW/milestone templates and ignore erroneous Appendix D references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposers' Day and information availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposer’s Day will now consist of a pre-recorded video that contains the relevant information for proposers. The link to the video will be emailed to all registrants and posted on SAM.gov and the PROSPR webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Proposers' Day recording and program materials posted to SAM.gov for clarifications and Q&A content.
